![Sol (max) places second on the Intelligence Index and first on the Coding Agent Index. Charts from [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center"}

[Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai) ran OpenAI's new GPT-5.6 family through its [pre-release evaluations](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed). The top model, Sol, scores one point below [Claude Fable 5](https://www.claude.com/) on the Intelligence Index at roughly a third of the cost, and the family fills out a new price-versus-intelligence frontier below it. Sol also tops the new Coding Agent Index at 80. Terra and Luna sit below Sol at progressively lower cost.

The family comes in three tiers. Sol is the flagship, the most capable and most expensive, at $5/$30 per million input/output tokens. Terra is the mid tier at $2.5/$15, and Luna the smallest and cheapest at $1/$6. All three are reasoning models with selectable effort, and GPT-5.6 adds a new max setting above the previous top. Raising the effort spends more tokens for more intelligence.

## What the Benchmarks Show

- **Intelligence Index**: Sol (max) scores 59, one point behind Fable 5 (60) and ahead of Opus 4.8 (56). Terra and Luna score 55 and 51. On the new Coding Agent Index, Sol leads at 80, with Terra and Luna at 77 and 75.

- **Cost**: Sol reaches near-parity at $1.04 per Intelligence Index task, about a third of Fable 5's $2.75 and below Opus 4.8's $1.80. Terra and Luna cost $0.55 and $0.21. Across reasoning-effort settings the family defines a new intelligence-versus-cost Pareto frontier, and each model beats GPT-5.5. Luna and Sol sit ahead of Terra at every effort level, so no Terra setting is worth choosing over the matching Luna or Sol one.

![Cost per task by token type, and the intelligence-versus-cost frontier. Charts from [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed).](chart-intelligence-cost.jpg){fig-align="center"}

- **Coding Agent Index (new)**: the index pairs each model with an agentic harness and averages three evaluations: DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench v2, and SWE-Atlas-QnA. Sol in [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) leads all three (tying Grok 4.5 in Grok Build on SWE-Atlas-QnA) at $7.08 per task, roughly 40% and 10% under Fable 5 and Opus 4.8 in [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code).

![Per-benchmark coding scores and cost per task. Charts from [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed).](chart-coding.jpg){fig-align="center"}

- **Token use**: Sol (max) spends 15k output tokens per task, just under GPT-5.5's 16k and well under Opus 4.8 (41k) and Claude Sonnet 5 (69k) while scoring higher, defining a new intelligence-versus-tokens frontier.

![Output tokens per task, and the intelligence-versus-tokens frontier. Charts from [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed).](chart-tokens.jpg){fig-align="center"}

- **Knowledge work (AA-Briefcase)**: on this agentic knowledge-work benchmark Sol ranks second to Fable 5 and posts the highest Presentation Elo of any model (1656), but Fable 5 keeps the top spot on Rubric Score (56% vs 42%) and Analytical Quality Elo (1764 vs 1592).

![AA-Briefcase combined Elo, and its analytical-quality and presentation components. Charts from [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed).](chart-briefcase.jpg){fig-align="center"}

- **Economically valuable tasks (GDPval-AA v2)**: Sol (1748) essentially ties Fable 5 (1760), both far above the 1,000 human baseline.

![GDPval-AA v2, anchored to a human baseline of 1,000. Chart from [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-5-6-has-landed).](chart-gdpval.jpg){fig-align="center"}

- **Knowledge reliability (AA-Omniscience)**: Sol edges past GPT-5.5 on accuracy (59%), but its hallucination rate climbs to 89%.

- **Cache-write pricing**: GPT-5.6 keeps OpenAI's 90% cache-read discount but is the first OpenAI family to charge for cache writes, at 1.25x the input price, matching Anthropic.

## My Notes

- **Cost is the deciding variable now.** When the top model trails Fable 5 by a single Intelligence Index point, quality stops driving the choice and price does. Sol's lower cost comes partly from spending fewer output tokens, and per-task cost climbs with the tokens each turn re-sends, the growth law [The Math Behind the Cost of AI Agents](/posts/20260513-the-math-behind-the-cost-of-ai-agents/) derives.

- **The coding lead is model-plus-harness.** Sol's 80 is measured in Codex, OpenAI's own harness, and the index pairs each model with a harness by design, so the ranking credits the pairing. A different harness moves both the score and the per-task cost, an effect [Databricks measured directly on its own codebase](/posts/20260713-databricks-coding-agent-benchmark/), which makes a cross-model coding claim hard to read as a statement about the model by itself.

- **Cache-write pricing is the structural change.** The new cache-write charge is a small line item, but it reprices long-context agentic workloads, which write large prompts to cache on nearly every turn. It also puts a price on the memory that agentic inference leans on, the resource [The Inference Shift](/posts/20260511-the-inference-shift/) argues becomes the binding constraint once no human is waiting on the model.

- **These are pre-release numbers.** Artificial Analysis discloses that it ran the evaluation before launch in coordination with OpenAI. The scores still come from a third party running its own index, and the pre-release arrangement is context worth having when reading them. [How Artificial Analysis Builds Its Intelligence Index](/posts/20260620-intelligence-benchmarking/) covers what the index does and does not capture.
